City health officials are issuing cautions to the public.

articles.headlineTranslated: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine for a high-fatality Nipah virus begins clinical trials in Belgium
articles.summary: Japan-developed Nipah virus vaccine, using a live-attenuated measles virus vector carrying Nipah genes, began clinical trials in Belgium on June 15, testing safety and immunogenicity in 60 healthy adults. Nipah virus, transmitted from fruit bats to people (and occasionally via human contact), can cause fever and myalgia and may progress to encephalitis with high fatality; there are no approved treatments or vaccines. The vaccine showed safety and efficacy in animal studies. If safety and immune response are confirmed, trials are planned in Bangladesh, where Nipah outbreaks occur. The project is led by Misako Yoneda of Teikyo University, with collaborators including the European Vaccine Initiative, Stanford University, and Japan’s Center for Advanced Research and Development Strategy. Researchers describe this as a potential step toward a practical vaccine against a deadly, zoonotic infection.

articles.summary: Measles infection confirmed in Kumamoto City, Japan, involving a teenage girl. Nationwide measles transmission is reported, with Kumamoto City Public Health Center noting no current evidence of broader spread. On June 1, it was learned that a person who had contact with the patient outside the prefecture had developed measles by June 3. The Kumamoto teenager self-observed at home from June 3; she developed mild fever and rash and tested positive on June 12. She is believed to have been infectious from the day before symptom onset to three days after fever onset, but she did not leave home during that period. Public health authorities state the infection does not appear to be expanding at present. Vaccination remains the most effective prevention against measles.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas: a quick refresher on what kind of disease it is.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading in the Tokyo metropolitan area and urban Kansai areas, likely surpassing the 2019 peak. Those in their late teens to 30s form the outbreak core, with immunity lower among this group than among 50s+ who had natural exposure, making measles a concern for young adults as well as children. After a 10–12 day incubation, patients develop fever (~38°C), cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; the catarrhal stage is the most contagious, with transmission risk near 100% for susceptible contacts and possible infection after a 30-minute room exposure. A subsequent fever spike (≥39°C) accompanies a characteristic red rash that starts on the neck or forehead and spreads to the body; pneumonia and encephalitis risk rise. Contagiousness persists for three days after fever subsides. Vaccination is the most reliable prevention: one dose is >95% effective; two doses are recommended. If immunity history is unknown, check with a blood test.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection in a man in Toyama Prefecture; overseas travel history; since November 2007.
articles.summary: Measles infection reported in a man in his 20s residing in the Takaoka Public Health Center area of Toyama Prefecture, Japan. It is the first measles case in Toyama since November 2019 amid a domestic outbreak. The patient developed fever on the 3rd and visited a Toyama medical facility on the 12th; infection was confirmed by genetic testing at the prefectural Public Health Laboratory and he remains under treatment. He had traveled to Indonesia about three days before onset, an area with higher measles exposure risk. Measles presents with fever and cough and can lead to pneumonia, otitis media, or encephalitis; most patients recover within 7–10 days. Two scheduled routine vaccinations are administered at age 1 and before entering elementary school; authorities urge vaccination to prevent further spread.

articles.summary: Measles infection confirmed in a man in his 20s within the Takaoka Public Health Center jurisdiction, Toyama Prefecture—the first measles case in Toyama since 2019 (seven years). The patient developed fever on June 3 and a rash; laboratory confirmation by the Prefectural Institute of Public Health; he is hospitalized. He had recently traveled to Indonesia, where measles transmission is ongoing, and investigators are determining the infection source and transmission route. Measles is highly contagious via airborne and droplet spread; in unimmunized individuals, illness begins with fever and cough, then a high fever (≥39°C) and rash lasting 4–5 days. The contagious period spans from one day before symptom onset to about three days after fever subsides. The prefecture urges caution and advises contacting healthcare facilities by phone before visiting if measles is suspected.

Experts attribute the surge to reduced vaccination during the COVID-19 era and ongoing vaccine hesitancy, lowering population immunity. Measles can cause pneumonia and otitis media; encephalitis occurs in about 1 in 1,000 cases, with mortality rates similar to those in developed countries. The WHO warns of a global resurgence, noting the virus is highly contagious. In context, the article cites Bangladesh as experiencing substantial deaths, illustrating severe outcomes in lower-resource settings. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

articles.headline: 命に関わる重篤な合併症リスクも......驚異的な感染力を持つ麻しん（はしか）のリスクと、取るべき対策法
articles.headlineTranslated: Life-threatening risk of severe complications as well... the measles, with its astonishing contagiousness, and the measures to be taken.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading rapidly in Japan and worldwide, driven by its exceptionally high transmissibility (R0 12–18) and airborne spread. A single unimmunized person can infect up to 18 others; in households, about 90% of susceptible contacts become infected. The illness begins with a catarrhal phase (1–4 days) of fever 38–39°C, runny nose, cough and conjunctivitis, followed by a high fever and widespread rash during the eruption phase. Complications include pneumonia and, in about 1 in 1,000 cases, encephalitis; long-term sequelae and SSPE can occur years later. In Japan, outbreaks have surged: 45 cases in 2024, 265 in 2025, and 462 cases by week 18 of 2026 (through May 3), concentrated in urban areas such as Tokyo and Aichi, affecting adults over 20. Vaccination coverage remains below 95% (first dose 92.7%, second dose 91.0% in 2024). An emergency vaccination program for contacts started May 18, 2026. MR vaccine (two doses) offers 97–99% protection; one dose 93–95%.

articles.headlineTranslated: Editorial: Measles Outbreak — Discard the Old Understanding of the Disease
articles.summary: Measles cases rise in Japan, with 498 reported in Tokyo and other cities by May 17, 2026, approaching the 2019 peak of 744. Although not yet confirmed in this prefecture, containment is critical. Measles causes fever, cough, runny nose, and rash about 10 days after exposure and is highly contagious—up to 10 times influenza—with potential encephalitis. There is no specific antiviral therapy. Japan was declared measles-elimination by WHO in 2015, but importations from travelers sustain transmission during a surge. Vaccination remains the most effective defense: one dose ~95% protection; two doses >99%. First-dose coverage fell from ≥95% to 90% in 2024; second-dose has remained below 95% since 2022. Most cases are aged 10–40; those born before 2000-04-01 may lack two doses. Check immunization records, consider antibody testing or voluntary vaccination if uncertain. After the long holiday, cases may rise; contact a provider before visiting if measles is suspected.

articles.headlineTranslated: Fukuoka City forms Infectious Disease Crisis Management Expert Committee; measles outbreak, hantavirus outbreak, affecting 20 healthcare workers.
articles.summary: Fukuoka City forms Infectious Disease Crisis Management Expert Committee as nationwide measles outbreaks and hantavirus detected on an Atlantic Ocean cruise ship raise concerns. The gathering aligns with concerns over measles activity nationwide and a hantavirus case on an Atlantic cruise ship. On May 25, about 20 healthcare professionals gathered at Fukuoka City Hall to discuss emergency coordination and strengthen information sharing for potential contingencies. Proceedings were closed to the press. This year, nationwide measles cumulative cases reached 479 as of May 13. The meeting underscores local readiness to respond to overseas-origin infectious disease events, with emphasis on inter-agency collaboration and rapid information exchange to prevent and manage outbreaks.

articles.headlineTranslated: In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccine hesitancy? ... Measles vaccination rate has fallen; Fukui Prefecture says "the most effective preventive measure to curb the spread of infection" | Medical | News from Fukui | Fukui Shimbun ONLINE
articles.summary: Measles vaccination rates in Fukui Prefecture have fallen below the 95% herd-immunity target, with two-dose MR (measles-rubella) vaccination administered at ages 12–24 months and before entering elementary school (5–7). In 2024, first-dose coverage was 92.6% and second-dose 92.4%; earlier years saw declines (2022 second dose 92.1%; 2023 and 2024 slipping below 95% for the first or second dose). National measles cases reached 479 as of May 13, 2026, the second-highest pace in the past decade after 2019; Fukui has recorded one infection last year and one this year. A 40-year-old man in Fukui contracted measles after traveling to Vietnam in late April. Measles is highly infectious via airborne, droplet, and contact transmission; incubation about 10 days; symptoms start with fever and cough, then high fever and rash, with pneumonia or otitis media risk. Vaccination reduces disease risk and severity.
